text:
Maria B: quick check — noticed streaming responses from hosted/api sometimes arrive as a bunch of tiny chunks after token refresh, then client JSON parser sees partial objects and stalls. anyone seen auth refresh -> backpressure amplification?

Kevin L: yup, seen this in prod traces. when our auth refresh flow races, we end up re-opening the SSE connection a few times in quick succession. server sends small seq of bytes while handshake finishes, client incremental parser treats them as fragmented JSON and waits.

Jon P: can you paste a tiny repro log?

Maria B: here's the short flow:
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:01Z] token_expiry -> start refresh
[2026-03-15T10:02:01Z] new request arrives -> SDK triggers refresh too (concurrent)
[2026-03-15T10:02:01Z] sdk reconnect -> keepalive chunks: "{\n"
[2026-03-15T10:02:02Z] partial data: \"id\": 123, \"text\": \"hello
[2026-03-15T10:02:03Z] final chunk: \"}\n"
```
Client parser sees JSON open but incomplete for ~1s and then emits partial error or stalls.

Sam R: sounds like two problems: (1) stale/duplicate refresh calls; (2) small chunk emission from server during connection warmup. Debounce token refresh so only one inflight. Also treat incremental parser as streaming NDJSON — assemble by bracket counting or use a small buffer timeout before failing.

Kevin L: agree. For JS SDK we implemented a tiny debounce + queue: if refresh in progress, wait on the same promise instead of starting another refresh. gist:
```
let _refreshPromise = null;
async function refreshToken() {
  if (_refreshPromise) return _refreshPromise;
  _refreshPromise = doRefresh().finally(() => { _refreshPromise = null; });
  return _refreshPromise;
}
```
This cut concurrent reconnects by ~95%.

Jon P: good. On parser side we added a 40ms micro-batch window: collect incoming text frames into buffer, attempt JSON parse when balanced braces or timeout. Prevents flakey partial-json errors and reduces churn on event loop.

Maria B: any concerns about added latency? we care about tail p50 for streaming.

Sam R: micro-batching 20–50ms is usually fine; it aggregates tiny bursts into a single parse. We only do it for streams where messages are full JSON objects (SSE/ndjson). For the chat streaming path we keep immediate forwarding for text tokens.

CI-Bot: rollout plan posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/567 — JS SDK patch adds refresh debounce + stream buffer window. Will run canary on dedicated env.

Kevin L: +1. Also add a metric for "auth_refresh_fanout" — counts how many refresh attempts happen within 2s windows per client id. Helps see client-side races.

Jon P: test ideas: simulate 50 concurrent requests at token expiry; assert only 1 refresh call, and assert stream messages parsed without json exceptions. Add a deterministic fake clock to avoid flakiness.

Maria B: created a short local repro script (node) — will paste in the PR and mark reviewers. Need someone to review parser debounce logic.

Sam R: I'll take parser review tomorrow morning. Also suggest adding server-side calming: on new connection during refresh, hold emitting full JSON until KV cache warmed to avoid many tiny frames.

Kevin L: added a note in the PR about server-side gating. Not blocking but a nice optimization.

Maria B: thanks all. tagging for visibility: @Jon P @Kevin L @Sam R — will drop follow-up in #eng-runtime once canary looks good. :thumbsup:
